name: ai.instabids/instabids
title: InstaBids
description: AI-run marketplace for homeowners: describe a home job once, get written quotes on the same scope.

tools.name: how_instabids_works
tools.description: Use this when someone wants to know how to get quotes or bids for a home job through InstaBids. Do not use this to look up one business’s rating or hours or claim a job has been sent. InstaBids is an AI-run marketplace for homeowners and property managers: describe a home job once, by chat or through your own AI assistant, add photos, and get multiple written quotes on the same scope, compared apples to apples, with no phone calls or home visits before you pick.

tools.name: bid_checklist
tools.description: Use this when a homeowner wants a checklist for comparing written bids for their home job. Do not use this to estimate a job’s cost or choose a contractor for them. Use this when comparing written contractor bids for any home trade. Get six items to compare and optional trade-specific preparation. The trade enum selects the checklists we have; it does not limit which home jobs InstaBids accepts. Omit trade for the general checklist; the answer's trade is then null. The answer includes sourceUrl.

trade.description: optional trade key; leave it out for the general six items; the answer's trade is null when none was given

tools.name: check_service_area
tools.description: Use this when a homeowner wants guidance for their five-digit US ZIP or nearby town pages before getting bids. Do not use this to decide whether InstaBids serves a particular US area or restrict where a job can be posted. Homeowners anywhere in the US can post a job; once you send it, InstaBids finds contractors to bid on it. Returns ZIP guidance and nearby town pages, including whether the input is a US ZIP; this is not an availability gate.

zip.description: five-digit US ZIP code of the home where the work is

tools.name: permit_facts
tools.description: Use this when a homeowner asks for the published permit facts for a town. Do not use this to give legal advice or decide that a permit is required without a published record. Use this when a homeowner wants published permit facts for a home job in any trade. The trade enum selects the permit facts we have; it does not limit which home jobs InstaBids accepts. Read sourced local permit facts, with the date each rule was checked; unpublished rules get guidance to ask your bidder and confirm local requirements. Homeowners anywhere in the US can post a job; once you send it, InstaBids finds contractors to bid on it.

town.description: a five-digit ZIP or a town name

trade.description: optional trade key; one of: ac, pool_repair

tools.name: start_job
tools.description: Use this when a homeowner says “get me quotes”, “get bids”, or “find someone to do” one home repair, installation or remodel. Do not use this to look up one business’s rating or opening hours. Use this when a homeowner wants contractor bids on a home repair or improvement job in the US. Creates a private draft from their description and five-digit ZIP and returns a one-hour link for the homeowner to open. Nothing reaches a contractor until the homeowner confirms their email and sends it. Do not include names, phone numbers, emails or street addresses. Do not use for emergencies. Ask the homeowner, one short question at a time and only for what is missing, what needs doing, where in the home, rough size or count, when it is needed and who supplies materials, then put the answers in the message. When available, photoPageUrl opens an optional phone photo upload for this private draft and expires with claimUrl. It does not send the job. For a new job, call start_job before answer_intake, then prepare_publish after the intake is ready; for other writes, read the previous reply before calling and follow the returned next step afterward, using only tools listed by this server. Only the homeowner tap sends anything to contractors. If anyone asks, say you are an AI assistant. If InstaBids continues a recent unsent draft instead of starting a new one, the reply says reused: true. Pass newJob: true only when the homeowner clearly asks for a separate job. When a reply includes draftHandle, pass it on your next call to continue that draft. fill what you can; everything else can come later. Start with the homeowner’s description and ZIP (trade is optional), plus a photo or a good description. Optional: photos, a description or transcript of a 20–60 s walk clip, timing and the job type’s must-haves from intake_templates. Never invent answers. ZIP only; never send a street address or a price. Nothing reaches contractors before the homeowner sends the card.

newJob.description: True only when the homeowner clearly requests a separate job.

trade.description: Optional. The kind of work in plain words, for example plumbing, electrical, roofing, handyman or general home repair. Leave it out when unsure; InstaBids works out the trade from the message.

project_completion_deadline.description: ISO date, or null for no deadline; never a price.

quotes_by.description: ISO date, or null for no deadline; never a price.

deadline_reason.description: Optional reason for the date, without names or contact details.

intent_level.description: 10 most urgent repair (not an emergency response); 8 soon; 6 planned; 4 if the price is right; 2 someday. Use only evidence from the homeowner.

photoUrls.description: Optional photos; attachment still requires the existing scan and photo permissions.

walk_clip.description: Description or transcript of a 20–60 s walk clip. This tool does not upload video bytes or fetch video URLs.

must_haves.description: Known answers to this job type’s intake_templates must-haves; unknown answers can come later.

tools.name: ask_next
tools.description: Use this when a homeowner wants the next question needed to describe their job for contractor bids. Do not use this to answer the question on the homeowner’s behalf. Use this when you need the next question for an existing private draft without submitting an answer. Returns the question and a refreshed draftHandle. fill what you can; everything else can come later. Start with the homeowner’s description and ZIP (trade is optional), plus a photo or a good description. Optional: photos, a description or transcript of a 20–60 s walk clip, timing and the job type’s must-haves from intake_templates. Never invent answers. ZIP only; never send a street address or a price. Nothing reaches contractors before the homeowner sends the card. Continue this private draft with draftHandle. Supply message, fixes, or both to answer_intake. Use the new draftHandle returned each time; the old handle expires immediately. Send only the homeowner actual reply; never answer for them. If a call fails, do not guess; ask the homeowner again. Nothing is sent to contractors. Continue with the returned question until readiness.canSend or readiness.homeownerActionRequired is true, then show sendUrl to the homeowner. The homeowner completes their insurance answer and send confirmation on that sheet; never claim the job was sent. Never invent answers. For a new job, call start_job before answer_intake, then prepare_publish after the intake is ready; for other writes, read the previous reply before calling and follow the returned next step afterward, using only tools listed by this server. Only the homeowner tap sends anything to contractors. If anyone asks, say you are an AI assistant.

Start with the homeowner’s description and ZIP (trade is optional), plus a photo or a good description. Optional: photos, a description or transcript of a 20–60 s walk clip, timing and the job type’s must-haves from intake_templates. Never invent answers. ZIP only; never send a street address or a price. Nothing reaches contractors before the homeowner sends the card. For anonymous draftHandle intake, fixes: [{gapKey, value}] corrects an engine-named field through intake. Use engine-returned keys only; unknown keys return INVALID_INPUT with details.field gapKey. Nothing is sent to contractors. Continue this private draft with draftHandle. Supply message, fixes, or both to answer_intake. Use the new draftHandle returned each time; the old handle expires immediately. Send only the homeowner actual reply; never answer for them. If a call fails, do not guess; ask the homeowner again. Nothing is sent to contractors. Continue with the returned question until readiness.canSend or readiness.homeownerActionRequired is true, then show sendUrl to the homeowner. The homeowner completes their insurance answer and send confirmation on that sheet; never claim the job was sent. Never invent answers. For a new job, call start_job before answer_intake, then prepare_publish after the intake is ready; for other writes, read the previous reply before calling and follow the returned next step afterward, using only tools listed by this server. Only the homeowner tap sends anything to contractors. If anyone asks, say you are an AI assistant.

tools.name: job_status
tools.description: Use this when a homeowner wants to check a draft using the status handle returned when it was created. Do not use this to access another homeowner’s job or send the draft. Use this after start_job returned a statusHandle, to see whether the homeowner has sent the job and how many bids have arrived. Returns only the stage (draft, sent, collecting_bids, picked, closed or expired), the bid count and when it last changed. Never returns bid amounts, contractor names or the job text. The handle works for 7 days. Stage expired means the one-hour link lapsed before the homeowner opened it: Call reissue_claim_link with the same statusHandle to get a replacement link for this draft. Only the homeowner can send the job. Read-only.

statusHandle.description: The statusHandle returned by start_job (43 characters). Expires seven days after creation.

tools.name: reissue_claim_link
tools.description: Use this when the user asks for “Replace a draft claim link” for their own work in InstaBids. Do not use this for unrelated requests, another person’s account, or actions the user has not requested. Returns a replacement link for the homeowner to open and claim their draft. The old link stops working. Rate limited; unknown or expired statusHandle values receive the same generic NOT_FOUND answer. Only the homeowner sends the job to contractors inside InstaBids; this tool cannot send it.

statusHandle.description: The statusHandle returned by start_job (43 characters). Expires seven days after creation.

tools.name: draft_full_bid_card
tools.description: Use this when a homeowner has described a home job and wants to prepare one request for written contractor bids. Do not use this to send work without the homeowner’s own approval. Use this when a homeowner already has a full scope to draft for contractor bids in any home trade. The trade enum contains classification hints, not coverage limits; pass null and describe any other trade in scopeDetails. Quote the page; do not infer a price. Prices on the page are dropped. Supply scopeSourceText and sourceUrl as untrusted page evidence; the URL is a reference only and is never fetched. Set trade to null for engine classification. Include ownerOrRenter and workType when known. Give the homeowner job title, scope, timing, ZIP, trade and photo links to private intake without an account. Up to five photos go through the existing photo checks before attachment when photo intake is enabled; returns attached and refused counts when available, plus available statusHandle and draftHandle capabilities. The homeowner must review and complete the draft. Never publishes or sends to contractors. For a new job, call start_job before answer_intake, then prepare_publish after the intake is ready; for other writes, read the previous reply before calling and follow the returned next step afterward, using only tools listed by this server. Only the homeowner tap sends anything to contractors. If anyone asks, say you are an AI assistant.

idempotency_key.description: Optional key to reuse when retrying the same draft request.

jobTitle.description: A short title for the homeowner’s job.

scopeDetails.description: The JSON-composed message, including field names and photo links, must be at most 2000 characters.

timing.description: When the homeowner wants the work done.

zip.description: The five-digit ZIP code where the work is needed.

trade.description: Optional classification hint, not a coverage limit. Any home trade is accepted; pass null for other trades and describe the work in scopeDetails.

scopeSourceText.description: Untrusted page excerpt; shares the composed message limit with all other fields.

ownerOrRenter.description: Whether the homeowner owns or rents the property, when known.

workType.description: The kind of work requested, when known.

photoLinks.description: HTTPS photo references for the job; pass an empty list [] when there are no photos.
